title: Limestone National - Data Residency & Compliance Discovery
summary: Initial discovery focused on data residency and compliance requirements for possible Redwood deployment. Customer is evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private due to EU/US data residency needs, PCI/HIPAA adjacency, and strict logging restrictions for production PII. Roadmap: send security package, schedule technical deep dive and canary PoC with dedicated capacity, and prepare draft SOW/pricing.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
Network egress, VPC peering, and air-gapped on-prem options
action_items: Alex Moreno (AE): Send SOC2 report, security pack, and network diagram by 2026-03-06

Sofia Ruiz (Customer): Provide sample retention policy and redaction requirements (PII fields) — due 2026-03-08
next_steps: Redwood to send security pack + SOC2 + ISO docs

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 42 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Alex Moreno (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Redwood CSM); Evelyn Carter (CISO), Mark Daniels (CTO), Sofia Ruiz (Head of Compliance), Tom Nguyen (Platform Lead)

Summary (auto): quick discovery on data residency and compliance. Customer wants EU-only residency for EU customers, strict logging controls, need for KMS/HSM, and validation that hosted API does not send logs or PII outside region. Exploring dedicated/reserved capacity vs private deployment for regulatory boundary.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining — I'm Alex from Redwood, Priya is our solutions engineer, Jordan's on for success. Quick round robin?
[00:12] Evelyn (CISO): Evelyn here, I'll be driving the compliance side. We've got Mark our CTO and Sofia for regulatory.
[00:18] Mark (CTO): Hi all.
[00:20] Priya (Redwood SE): Great, thanks. Agenda I have is residency requirements, logging/retention, key mgmt, then trade-offs between hosted/dedicated/private. Sound good?
[00:30] Sofia (Compliance): Sounds right. Just so you know, Limestone handles EU customer data and US customer data; for EU-resident accounts we need data and logs to stay in EU per GDPR, also need processing agreement and SCCs or equivalent.
[00:45] Alex: Understood. Quick question — do you already have some sort of in-region cloud footprint?
[00:50] Tom (Platform): Yes, we run prod services in AWS eu-west-1 and have a private VPC. We prefer no customer data leaving EU for EU customers.
[01:05] Priya: We can do region pinning and route requests to EU-hosted Redwood infra. For Hosted API we offer EU-only endpoints, but some enterprise controls (audit logs, advanced KMS options) are richer on Dedicated or Private — just calling that out.
[01:25] Sofia: For us audit logs are odd — we have to redact certain fields and we have retention windows mandated by regulators. Can Redwood do selective log redaction before logs are stored?
[01:40] Priya: Yes, we have log redaction rules at the ingestion point and you can configure which token streams are persisted. On hosted we can enable PII redaction, but for the strictest control customers choose Dedicated or Private so they manage the logging pipeline themselves.
[01:58] Mark: If we do Dedicated, is the KMS keys customer managed? We need to ensure key custody — can't have Redwood hold keys for EU data.
[02:10] Alex: Dedicated supports customer-managed KMS for most cloud providers, and Private gives full HSM/KMS integration for on-prem. We'll capture the exact providers in the follow up.
[02:24] Sofia: HIPAA — not core but some of our business lines touch health-adjacent data. Do you have BAAs?
[02:32] Alex: We do offer HIPAA support for enterprise customers; we can share the BAA sample in the security pack.
[02:38] Tom: Network wise, we need VPC peering or private link and strict egress controls. Any outbound requests to non-EU telemetry or model registries?
[02:50] Priya: For Hosted we may call model artifact stores that are region-bound; we can keep those in EU. For telemetry we have options to disable telemetry or send it to your syslog via private connectivity on Dedicated/Private. There is a small chance of metadata services calling home for control-plane features — we can scrub that or route it through your private control plane on Private deployments.
[03:12] Evelyn: Can you confirm audit log retention range and if we can set retention to 90 days for logs and then automatic purge?
[03:20] Priya: Yes, retention policies are configurable; on Hosted there's a default retention and we can request custom retention via enterprise plan. On Dedicated/Private you control retention in your own logging stack.
[03:35] Mark: Performance — if we pin to EU region, what's the latency impact? We have 200ms p95 requirement for chat latency for certain customer flows.
[03:45] Priya: Depends on model size and sequence length; Dedicated gives predictable throughput and lower tail latency due to reserved GPU pools. Hosted EU endpoints are performant but shared multitenant workloads can add variance. For strict p95 SLOs we recommend Dedicated with reserved capacity.
[04:05] Sofia: About SGX/HSM — can you integrate with our HSM for key sign/verify?
[04:12] Priya: Private deployment supports HSM integrations. Dedicated supports customer-managed KMS (cloud KMS) but not necessarily on-prem HSM. We'll put specifics in the security doc.
[04:25] Alex: Quick clarifying question: when you say "EU-only", do you mean both inference and logs must stay in EU, or just customer data?
[04:33] Sofia: Both. And logs containing PII need to be redacted or never leave region.
[04:40] Priya: Noted. We'll validate our Hosted EU isolation and provide a data flow diagram showing where logs live and retention.
[04:52] Tom: Also need SSO — SAML + SCIM for provisioning, RBAC that maps to our AD groups.
[05:00] Alex: We support SAML SSO and SCIM for provisioning and customizable RBAC. On Private you can run the control plane inside your network and bind to AD as well.
[05:10] Mark: Any data residency limitations with model updates? If Redwood pulls model updates from upstream non-EU repos, will that cause egress?
[05:20] Priya: We can host model artifacts in-region. For major open models we have EU-hosted model variants; we'll verify the artifact sources.
[05:30] Evelyn: How about legal — DPA, SCCs, and audit rights? We need to be able to audit logs and have contractual commitments on data handling.
[05:42] Alex: We'll include our DPA and standard SCCs in the security pack and flag any items for negotiation in SOW. We also provide audit logs and can set up a recurring export to your logging stack for audit purposes.
[05:55] Sofia: One nuanced ask: regulators sometimes require that logs containing masked PII still be reversible only under legal process. We need key escrow or split custody. Is that supported?
[06:08] Priya: That's more advanced; Private gives the most flexibility. For Dedicated we can integrate with your KMS where you control key lifecycle; split custody patterns might need architectural review.
[06:22] Tom: For the PoC we want to validate two things: EU pinning with logs stored in EU and log redaction rules, plus end-to-end latency for our 512-token chat flows. Can we get a two-week dedicated trial?
[06:35] Alex: Yes, we can provision a short reserved environment for PoC — typically 1-2 weeks. We'll need expected QPS and model family to size.
[06:44] Mark: We're looking at about 10 rps steady, 50 rps bursts, and model family similar to open Llama-style medium. Latency SLO 200ms p95.
[06:58] Priya: That helps. We'll size a couple of GPUs and include batching configs. We'll also surface quantization and perf recommendations.
[07:10] Sofia: Logging retention: is it possible to only store hashes for certain fields and drop raw text?
[07:18] Priya: Yes, token-level hashing and redaction can be applied; on Hosted we have prebuilt rules, Dedicated/Private give you full control to implement custom redaction.
[07:30] Evelyn: Encryption at rest — do you encrypt with customer keys in EU?
[07:36] Alex: For Dedicated and Private yes. Hosted enterprise can support CMEK (customer-managed encryption keys) with cloud provider KMS in-region. We will confirm exact providers supported.
[07:48] Mark: What about log egress to third-party monitoring? We push logs to Splunk via forwarder; any issue?
[07:56] Priya: We can forward logs to your Splunk instance via private connection, or you can pull logs from our export. For EU data, we'd keep outbound within EU endpoints.
[08:10] Tom: Are there any regulatory certifications — SOC2, ISO 27001?
[08:14] Alex: We are SOC2 Type II and working on ISO 27001; full details in security pack.
[08:21] Sofia: Can we redact at inference time so transcripts do not store PII? Example: customer submits SSN in prompt, we must ensure model output doesn't echo that back into persisted logs.
[08:33] Priya: We have moderation/redaction filters and can apply transformation hooks pre-persist. We'll show how to set up a pre-persist hook in the PoC.
[08:45] Evelyn: Legal may ask about eDiscovery — can you produce logs in a forensic format for audits?
[08:52] Alex: Yes, audit exports can be formatted to meet eDiscovery needs; we'll include sample export schemas.
[09:00] Mark: Cost — Dedicated vs Hosted cost delta? If we commit to Dedicated, what's the pricing model?
[09:08] Alex: Dedicated is reserved monthly capacity with commit tiers, different from per-token hosted. We'll follow up with a preliminary pricing sheet based on the PoC sizing.
[09:19] Tom: Any constraints on storing embeddings and vectors within EU? We store user embeddings for retrieval — must be EU-only.
[09:28] Priya: Embedding storage is treated as data; we can host vector stores in-region or integrate with your vector DB in your VPC for full control.
[09:36] Sofia: One more — data deletion: regulators require deletion within X days on request. Can you support immediate deletion and cert?
[09:44] Alex: Yes, deletions are supported; we'll provide processes and a deletion certificate. For Hosted, we'll document timelines; Dedicated/Private you own the data lifecycle.
[09:56] Mark: Ok great. Next steps?
[10:00] Alex: We'll assemble the security pack (SOC2, DPA, SCCs, technical diagrams), propose PoC sizing, and schedule an SE technical deep dive to scope Dedicated/Private options. We'll also send pricing draft.
[10:12] Sofia: Expect review from Legal and Compliance; we'll want to see data flow diagrams and the BAA.
[10:18] Alex: Noted. Anything else from Redwood?
[10:22] Priya: I'll follow up with an agenda for the technical deep dive and notes on KMS/HSM integration.
[10:28] Tom: We'll send infra diagram and compliance checklist.
[10:32] Evelyn: Thanks everyone.
[10:34] Alex: Thanks all — we'll follow up early next week.

Notes on transcript quality: medium. Some audio cutouts and names may be mis-transcribed (e.g., Llama -> Llama-like models, KV cache as K-V cash at times).

References/Shared artifacts mentioned:
- Security pack (SOC2, DPA, SCCs) — link placeholder: https://redwood.example.com/security-pack/limestone
- PoC sizing spreadsheet (will be shared)
- Draft SOW/pricing (to be shared after sizing)

End of transcript.
